objective: Let the human load the NBA dataset into the live database: a private S3 bucket that holds the four CSVs, and a SportsDataLoad function on the shared backend image that downloads them and runs app.events.nba_history for the seasons it is given, invoked by hand only, with s3:GetObject on that bucket's nba-eoin/ prefix as its one grant beyond what every function has.
acceptance_criteria: Fanwire-Storage has a new SportsDataBucket, exposed as StorageStack.sportsDataBucket with a SportsDataBucketName output: SSE-KMS with the stack's existing CMK, all public access blocked, bucket-owner-enforced ownership, SSL enforced, not versioned, no lifecycle rule, no event notifications and no EventBridge, and named by no CloudFront origin, GuardDuty plan or other function's policy.

Fanwire-App has a SportsDataLoad function built by backendFunction on the shared image with command app.events.load_handler.handler, a 15-minute timeout, 2048 MB of memory and 1024 MB of ephemeral storage, and an environment of the common variables plus SPORTS_DATA_BUCKET set to the bucket's name.

SportsDataLoad's policy holds exactly backendFunction's three statements plus one, s3:GetObject on the bucket's nba-eoin/* objects: no s3:ListBucket, no write or delete action, no other bucket or prefix, and no grant to any other function on the bucket.

Nothing invokes SportsDataLoad: app-stack.test.ts's invoker sweep (no rule, schedule, event source mapping, permission or custom resource, in any stack) covers it as it covers Migration, and it has no async invoke config.

The IAM wildcard gate, the permissions-boundary test and cfn-exec-policy.test.ts pass with infra/iam/** unchanged; the stacks add no resource type the CloudFormation execution policy does not already grant.

app.events.load_handler.handler takes an event {"seasons": [...]}: a non-empty list of distinct YYYY-YY seasons from 2003-04 on. A missing, empty, non-list or malformed seasons value, or any other key in the event, raises before any S3 call or database connection.

With a valid event the handler downloads exactly Games.csv, PlayerStatistics.csv, TeamStatistics.csv and Players.csv from s3://$SPORTS_DATA_BUCKET/nba-eoin/ into a new temporary directory under the system temp dir, runs load_nba_history for those seasons, and returns the LoadReport as a JSON-serialisable dict; the temporary directory is removed whether the load succeeds or fails.

A missing object, an unset SPORTS_DATA_BUCKET or DATABASE_URL, a dataset error or an unknown team or player makes the invocation fail by raising, never by returning an error value, and leaves the database unchanged (the loader's one transaction).

Only one load runs at a time: the handler holds a Postgres advisory lock, distinct from app.migrate's, for the whole load, and a second load that cannot take it fails fast with a message saying a load is already running, writing nothing.

The database URL never leaves the function: not in a log line, the return value or the raised exception, whose cause is not chained to a database or loader exception that could carry it; a test with a password in DATABASE_URL and a failing connection proves it, using the same redaction as app.migrate.

wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x02-events.md documents the function and points to build-deployment.md "Load sports data", the runbook in single-line PowerShell steps (upload the four files to the bucket's nba-eoin/ prefix, find the function, write the event to a file, invoke it with a CLI read timeout above 15 minutes, read the report). The runbook itself is a Director PR: no unit role may write wiki/CodeContext/Standards/.
